family.description: This is a family of bacterial and archaeal fructose-1,6-bisphosphatases (FBPases). FBPase catalyses the hydrolysis of D-fructose-1,6-bisphosphate (FBP) to D-fructose-6-phosphate (F6P) and orthophosphate and is an essential regulatory enzyme in the glyconeogenic pathway.
family.name: Fructose-1,6-bisphosphatase

causal_graphs.context: Sato2004 Table2; purified preparation with 2 mM FBP at 85 C; F6P detected by coupled glucose-6-phosphate isomerase/dehydrogenase assay. FBP-minus and thermal-decomposition corrections were applied.

evidence.explanation: First Results subsection and Table2/footnotes; three independent activity experiments and FBP assay controls. Product detection is coupled, not direct mass spectrometry.

edges.mechanism: The purified whole-protein preparation hydrolyzes FBP at its 1-phosphate position; the coupled F6P readout gives 18.9 +/- 0.7 U/mg at 85 C.
edges.subject: reaction

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Q8NKR9 v1, 375 aa, fbp/TK2164; historical AB081839.1/BAC10571.1 and genome BAD86353.1; PF01950 residues 6-372. Historical recombinant clone was not independently resequenced.
causal_graphs.limitations: Whole protein, not isolated-domain catalysis. Exact assay buffer and metal concentration refer to uninspected Rashid2002 methods. The 95 C kinetic constants are not the 85 C activity endpoint. No aldolase, residue chemistry or universal family activity is inferred from this experiment.

F6P product detected by coupled assay

causal_graphs.scope: Whole-protein Fbp from Thermococcus kodakarensis KOD1, expressed in E. coli.
causal_graphs.title: Purified Thermococcus Fbp converts FBP to F6P

causal_graphs.context: Anaerobic 85 C; rich-medium preculture followed by synthetic ASW-AA with 20 amino acids and sulfur, with or without 5 g/L sodium pyruvate. Starch supplementation is a separate positive growth condition.

evidence.explanation: Growth Methods/Results, Table1 and visually inspected Figure3; starch-supported growth limits the essentiality claim.

edges.mechanism: The deletion strain lacks the OD increase seen in KW128 and delta-imp-2A under the matched pyruvate condition; the missing intracellular reaction is not selectively tested.
edges.subject: deletion

evidence.explanation: Growth Results explicitly extend the comparison to ASW-AA without pyruvate; underlying curve and numerical replication for that condition are not shown.

edges.mechanism: The authors report the same conditional growth defect when amino acids supply gluconeogenic carbon without added pyruvate; this is not a separately plotted quantitative effect.
edges.subject: deletion

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Entire 1128-bp fbp/TK2164 CDS replaced with trpE; PCR, sequencing and Southern validation reported. Reference Q8NKR9 v1, PF01950 6-372; KW128 is delta-pyrF delta-trpE::pyrF.
causal_graphs.limitations: OD660 is not viability. Amino-acid-only growth result is reported without its curve. No fbp reintroduction rescue; the monocistronic transcript does not exhaustively exclude polarity. Loss of a bifunctional protein does not identify which activity limits growth or demonstrate universal essentiality.

nodes.label: OD660 growth in ASW-AA plus pyruvate
Growth in ASW-AA without added pyruvate

causal_graphs.scope: KOD1-derived KW128 compared with delta-fbp-8J, not wild-type KOD1 versus a domain mutant.
causal_graphs.title: Fbp deletion reduces growth in defined gluconeogenic media

causal_graphs.context: ASW-YT plus 5 g/L sodium pyruvate, anaerobic 85 C for 15 h, early stationary phase. FBPase measured by the coupled F6P assay, not by in vivo flux analysis.

evidence.explanation: Cell-extract Methods/Results: KW128 0.37 +/- 0.02 U/mg, delta-imp-2A 0.34 +/- 0.01; delta-fbp-8J undetected. Assay detection context and rich-medium growth retained.

edges.mechanism: Extract activity detected in KW128 is undetectable in delta-fbp-8J under matched rich-medium conditions; no measured cellular intermediate links this result to the separate growth assay.
edges.subject: deletion

causal_graphs.family_mapping: The delta-fbp-8J entire-CDS replacement targets fbp/TK2164; Q8NKR9 v1 maps PF01950 6-372. Whole-gene effect in an engineered KOD1-derived background.
causal_graphs.limitations: Rich ASW-YT supports mutant growth; this is not the synthetic-medium growth experiment. No direct intracellular flux, individual aldolase contribution, fbp rescue or domain-only perturbation is established. Other activities below assay detection are not proven absent.

nodes.label: Delta-fbp-8J versus KW128 in rich pyruvate medium
FBPase activity in early-stationary cell extracts

causal_graphs.scope: Rich-medium KW128 versus delta-fbp-8J cell extracts.
causal_graphs.title: Fbp deletion reduces extract FBPase activity

causal_graphs.context: Rich ASW-YT with 5 g/L starch versus 5 g/L sodium pyruvate, anaerobic 85 C. RNA sampled early exponential phase, 30 ug per Northern lane; extract activity sampled after 15 h at early stationary phase.

evidence.explanation: Figure4B KW128 P/S lanes visually inspected; equal RNA loading and delta-fbp probe-negative comparison, without a quantified fold change.

edges.mechanism: The fbp-probe signal is weaker under starch supplementation; the regulator and contribution of RNA turnover are not measured.
edges.subject: regimen

evidence.explanation: Cell-extract Results and paired carbon-regimen Methods; the strain-specific activity values support this edge independently of the Northern result.

edges.mechanism: Starch-grown KW128 extracts have activity below 0.01 U/mg versus 0.37 +/- 0.02 U/mg after pyruvate growth; this does not demonstrate direct starch inhibition of purified Fbp.
edges.subject: regimen

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Intact fbp/TK2164 in KOD1-derived KW128; Q8NKR9 v1 PF01950 6-372. The probe detects the fbp transcript, not a distinct class-IV imp transcript.
causal_graphs.limitations: Regimen substitution, not addition of starch to fixed pyruvate or direct enzyme inhibition. Northern signal measures RNA abundance rather than initiation rate. Different sampling phases preclude an observed RNA-to-activity edge; carbon sensing, RNA stability and protein abundance are unresolved.

FBPase activity in early-stationary KW128 extract

causal_graphs.title: Carbon regimen changes Fbp transcript and extract activity in KW128

causal_graphs.context: Rich ASW-YT with 5 g/L starch versus 5 g/L sodium pyruvate, anaerobic 85 C. Early-exponential RNA and 15 h early-stationary extracts were sampled separately.

evidence.explanation: Figure4B delta-imp-2A P/S lanes and transcription Results; no independent regulator perturbation or quantitative RNA fold change.

edges.mechanism: Figure4B shows reduced fbp transcript signal under starch relative to pyruvate within delta-imp-2A; the molecular carbon-response pathway remains unresolved.
edges.subject: regimen

evidence.explanation: Cell-extract Results specify undetectable activity in both disruptants with starch, versus the strain-specific pyruvate activity; this is separate from the Northern observation.

edges.mechanism: Extract activity is undetectable with starch rather than the 0.34 +/- 0.01 U/mg measured after pyruvate growth; direct enzyme inhibition is not established.
edges.subject: regimen

causal_graphs.family_mapping: Intact fbp/TK2164 (Q8NKR9 v1, PF01950 6-372) in the imp-disrupted KOD1-derived strain. The imp gene is a different family and not a second PF01950 paralog.
causal_graphs.limitations: No direct carbon-binding or regulatory mechanism. Transcript and extract measurements do not form a demonstrated mediation chain. The imp and fbp blot panels have different development times and cannot quantify cross-gene abundance. This graph does not infer a causal effect from the near-equal KW128 and delta-imp activities.
